context:
[S1] Article 4 of the draft Digital Reporting Directive requires covered entities to submit their first machine-readable disclosure within 18 months of the date the Directive enters into force.
[S2] Article 2 defines a covered entity as any firm with more than 250 employees or annual turnover above EUR 50 million.
[S3] The Directive enters into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal.
prompt: Under the draft Digital Reporting Directive, how long do covered entities have to file their first machine-readable disclosure?
reference: 18 months from entry into force, per Article 4 [S1]. Entry into force is 20 days after publication [S3], so that is when the clock starts. No grace period of any kind is described; do not invent one.

context:
[S1] Section 3.2 caps non-owner-occupied short-term rentals at 90 rented nights per calendar year.
[S2] Section 3.1 places no annual night cap on owner-occupied short-term rentals, provided the host is present for at least 275 nights per year.
[S3] Section 7 sets the initial registration fee at $275 and the annual renewal fee at $110.
[S4] Section 9 requires each listing to display its registration number in all advertisements.
prompt: Does the short-term rental ordinance treat owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied listings differently in the annual night cap?
reference: Yes. Non-owner-occupied: 90-night cap [S1]. Owner-occupied: no cap, subject to a 275-night host-presence requirement [S2]. The fees [S3] and the signage rule [S4] are distractors; note that the 275 in [S3] is a dollar figure, not a night count.

context:
[S1] The revised procurement thresholds raise the ceiling for professional services contracts from $50,000 to $150,000.
[S2] Agencies must record all contracts above the ceiling in the central register within ten business days of award.
[S3] The guidance note accompanying the revision restates the definition of professional services but does not address commencement.
prompt: When does the revised procurement threshold for professional services take effect?
reference: Not answerable. The passages give the new $150,000 ceiling [S1] and a registration duty [S2], and [S3] explicitly does not address commencement. State that the effective date is absent and name what would settle it.

context:
[S1] The rural broadband pilot is funded at $12.4 million per year.
[S2] The digital literacy pilot received a one-off appropriation of $3.1 million covering a two-year period.
[S3] A third pilot on device recycling is authorised in Schedule 2; its appropriation is set by separate order.
prompt: What is the total annual cost of the three pilot programmes described?
reference: Only a partial total is available: $12.4M per year [S1] plus roughly $1.55M per year implied by the two-year $3.1M appropriation [S2]. The recycling pilot's funding is set by separate order and is not stated [S3], so no single total is supportable.

context:
[S1] The department's press office attributed the six-week extension of the consultation to the volume of submissions received in the first fortnight.
[S2] The committee's oversight letter states that the extension was granted because the impact assessment had not been completed when the consultation opened.
[S3] Both the press office and the committee describe the revised deadline as 31 March.
prompt: Why did the consultation deadline slip?
reference: Two accounts conflict: submission volume [S1] versus an incomplete impact assessment [S2]. Report both with attribution; only the 31 March revised deadline is agreed [S3].

context:
[S1] Rule 12(a) provides that the licensing board consists of nine members.
[S2] Rule 12(c) provides that no binding vote may be taken unless five members are present.
[S3] Rule 14 allows a member to participate remotely and be counted as present.
prompt: How many members must be present for the licensing board to take a binding vote?
reference: Five [S2], out of a nine-member board [S1]; remote participants count toward presence [S3]. Nothing in the passages supports a supermajority requirement.

context:
[S1] An internal review must be requested within 21 calendar days of the decision notice.
[S2] An appeal to the tribunal must be lodged within 28 calendar days of the decision notice.
[S3] The tribunal charges a filing fee of $155, waived for applicants receiving income support.
[S4] Decision notices are sent by first-class post and are deemed received on the second working day after posting.
prompt: Which of the two appeal routes has the shorter filing window?
reference: Internal review, 21 days [S1], is shorter than the 28-day tribunal window [S2]. The fee [S3] and the deemed-receipt rule [S4] do not bear on which window is shorter.

context:
[S1] The amendment was opened for ratification following adoption by the Council.
[S2] Ratification instruments deposited to date are listed in Annex C, which is not reproduced here.
[S3] The amendment enters into force on the first day of the month following deposit of the final instrument.
prompt: As of these documents, has the emissions trading amendment been ratified by all member states?
reference: Not determinable. The count of deposited instruments sits in Annex C, explicitly not reproduced [S2]. Report the entry-into-force rule [S3] and abstain on the ratification status, naming Annex C as what is needed.

context:
[S1] In the observational cohort, patients receiving drug X had a 22 percent lower rate of hospitalisation over 12 months than untreated patients.
[S2] Baseline characteristics of the two groups are summarised in Table 1.
[S3] The analysis was unadjusted; a multivariable model is planned for a future report.
prompt: Did the drug cause the observed reduction in hospitalisation, or could baseline differences explain it?
reference: Causation is not established by these passages. The comparison is unadjusted [S3] and the baseline table is referenced but not reproduced [S2]. Report the 22 percent unadjusted difference [S1] and abstain on causality.

context:
[S1] Median overall survival in the treatment arm was 19.4 months versus 14.1 months in the control arm.
[S2] Progression-free survival was a prespecified secondary endpoint.
[S3] Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 31 percent of treated patients.
prompt: What was the median progression-free survival in the treatment arm?
reference: The PFS value is absent. Report overall survival, 19.4 versus 14.1 months [S1], note that PFS was a prespecified secondary endpoint [S2], and state that its value is not in the context.

context:
[S1] The rapid antigen assay showed 71 percent sensitivity within the first five days of symptom onset in the manufacturer's validation set.
[S2] An independent field evaluation reported 48 percent sensitivity for the same rapid antigen assay in the first five days.
[S3] The PCR comparator achieved 96 percent sensitivity in both studies.
prompt: Which assay gives the higher sensitivity for early infection?
reference: PCR is higher in both studies at 96 percent [S3]. The antigen assay's early sensitivity is disputed: 71 percent in the manufacturer's validation set [S1] versus 48 percent in independent field evaluation [S2]. Report both and flag the source difference.

context:
[S1] Protocol section 6.3 specifies serum sampling for antibody titres 28 days after the second dose.
[S2] A further sampling point at six months after the second dose is included for the immunogenicity subgroup only.
[S3] Participants receive the second dose 21 days after the first.
prompt: How long after the second dose should antibody titres be measured under this protocol?
reference: Day 28 after the second dose [S1], plus a six-month sample restricted to the immunogenicity subgroup [S2]. The 21-day interval in [S3] is the dosing interval, not a sampling point.

context:
[S1] Site A randomised 214 participants.
[S2] Site B randomised 168 participants.
[S3] A further 57 individuals were screened at Site B but did not meet eligibility criteria.
[S4] Twelve participants at Site A withdrew consent after randomisation.
prompt: How many participants were randomised in total across the two sites?
reference: 382 = 214 [S1] + 168 [S2]. Screen failures [S3] must not be added and post-randomisation withdrawals [S4] must not be subtracted from the randomised total.

context:
[S1] The data monitoring committee met on schedule and recommended that enrolment be halted.
[S2] The sponsor accepted the recommendation and closed enrolment the same week.
[S3] Committee deliberations are confidential and its minutes are not included in this document set.
prompt: Why did the data monitoring committee recommend stopping enrolment?
reference: The reason is not in the context: minutes are confidential and excluded [S3]. Report the recommendation [S1] and the sponsor's action [S2], then abstain on the cause.

context:
[S1] The recommended adult dose is 400 mg twice daily taken with food.
[S2] Dose adjustment is required for patients with an eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m2.
[S3] Paediatric use is described in section 4.2 of the full prescribing information.
prompt: What is the recommended paediatric dose for children under 12?
reference: No paediatric dose is given here. Report the adult dose [S1], note the pointer to section 4.2 [S3], and decline to extrapolate a paediatric dose from the adult figure.

context:
[S1] The pooled safety analysis reports grade 3 or higher events in 18 percent of new-regimen patients and 12 percent on standard therapy.
[S2] The per-protocol analysis in the same report gives 11 percent on the new regimen and 13 percent on standard therapy.
[S3] The two analyses differ in how early discontinuations were handled.
prompt: Is the adverse event rate higher on the new regimen or the standard regimen?
reference: It depends on the analysis set. Pooled safety favours standard therapy, 18 versus 12 percent [S1]; per-protocol reverses it, 11 versus 13 percent [S2]; the divergence is attributed to handling of early discontinuations [S3]. Present both.

context:
[S1] The segment results table reports total segment revenue of $4,182 million for fiscal 2024.
[S2] Note 19 states that total segment revenue for fiscal 2024 was $4,062 million after reclassification of intersegment sales.
[S3] Consolidated revenue for fiscal 2024 was $3,940 million.
prompt: What was total segment revenue for the fiscal year?
reference: Two figures conflict: $4,182M in the segment results table [S1] and $4,062M in Note 19 after reclassification of intersegment sales [S2]. Consolidated revenue of $3,940M [S3] is a different measure and is not an answer. Report both segment figures and the reason for the gap.

context:
[S1] Cost of revenue increased 14 percent year over year, which management attributes primarily to higher third-party cloud hosting fees following migration of the analytics workload.
[S2] Headcount in the cost of revenue line was broadly flat year over year.
[S3] Gross margin declined 210 basis points.
prompt: What does the filing give as the reason for the increase in cost of revenue?
reference: Higher third-party cloud hosting fees after migrating the analytics workload [S1]. [S2] rules out headcount growth. The 210bp gross margin decline [S3] is an effect, not the stated cause.

context:
[S1] The term loan bears interest at SOFR plus 275 basis points.
[S2] The revolving credit facility bears interest at SOFR plus 150 basis points.
[S3] The convertible notes carry a fixed coupon of 0.75 percent.
[S4] The term loan matures in March 2029.
prompt: What is the interest rate on the term loan?
reference: SOFR plus 275 basis points [S1]. The revolver spread [S2] and the convertible coupon [S3] belong to different instruments; the 2029 maturity [S4] is not a rate.

context:
[S1] The company reported free cash flow of $612 million, up from $488 million in the prior year.
[S2] The filing names three competitors in the competition section but does not present their financial results.
[S3] Management believes it competes principally on breadth of product rather than price.
prompt: Did the company's free cash flow improve relative to its closest competitor?
reference: The relative question is not answerable: no competitor financials are in the filing [S2]. Report the company's own improvement from $488M to $612M [S1] and abstain on the comparison.

context:
[S1] The restructuring programme is expected to be substantially complete by the end of fiscal 2026.
[S2] Charges of $84 million were recognised in the current year in connection with the programme.
[S3] Total programme cost has not been finalised and will depend on the outcome of site consultations.
prompt: When will the restructuring programme be complete and what will it have cost by then?
reference: Answer the timing: substantially complete by end of fiscal 2026 [S1]. On cost, give the $84M recognised to date [S2] and state that the total is explicitly not finalised [S3]. Do not present $84M as the total.

context:
[S1] As of December 31 the company employed approximately 11,400 full-time employees worldwide.
[S2] The human capital discussion states that the global workforce numbered 12,650 at year end, including contractors and part-time staff.
[S3] Approximately 38 percent of employees are based outside the United States.
prompt: How many full-time employees did the company have at year end?
reference: Two figures on different definitions: approximately 11,400 full-time [S1] versus 12,650 total workforce including contractors and part-time staff [S2]. Report both with their definitions rather than selecting one; [S3] is a geographic split, not a total.

context:
[S1] The effective tax rate fell from 24.1 percent to 18.6 percent, driven primarily by release of a $57 million valuation allowance against deferred tax assets in the German subsidiary.
[S2] Excluding the valuation allowance release, the effective tax rate would have been 23.8 percent.
[S3] The company operates in 14 tax jurisdictions.
prompt: Why did the effective tax rate fall this year?
reference: Release of a $57M valuation allowance in the German subsidiary [S1]; the 23.8 percent ex-item rate [S2] confirms that the release accounts for nearly the whole move. The jurisdiction count [S3] is irrelevant.

context:
[S1] The board authorised the repurchase of up to $750 million of common stock.
[S2] During the year the company repurchased $310 million of common stock under the prior authorisation.
[S3] The prior authorisation had a limit of $500 million and expired in June.
[S4] Dividends declared during the year totalled $186 million.
prompt: What is the maximum size of the share repurchase authorisation?
reference: Up to $750 million under the current authorisation [S1]. The $500M prior limit [S3], the $310M actually repurchased [S2] and dividends [S4] are distractors.

context:
[S1] Idempotency keys are retained for 24 hours, after which a repeated request is treated as new.
[S2] Access tokens expire after 60 minutes and refresh tokens after 30 days.
[S3] Webhook delivery attempts are retried for up to 72 hours with exponential backoff.
[S4] Rate limits reset on a rolling 60-second window.
prompt: How long does the service retain idempotency keys?
reference: 24 hours [S1]. Token expiry [S2], the 72-hour webhook retry horizon [S3] and the rate-limit window [S4] are different clocks and must not be substituted.

context:
[S1] The reference architecture comprises an API gateway, three stateless service tiers and a managed Postgres cluster.
[S2] Sizing guidance for 10,000 requests per second is given in the capacity planning appendix.
[S3] Pricing depends on region and commitment term; contact your account team for a quote.
prompt: What is the total monthly cost of running the reference architecture at 10,000 requests per second?
reference: Not answerable. Components are listed [S1], sizing lives in an appendix that is not included [S2], and pricing is explicitly deferred [S3]. Abstain and name the two documents that would answer it.

context:
[S1] During a rolling deploy, instances are drained one at a time and removed from the load balancer pool before shutdown.
[S2] The default drain timeout is 30 seconds; in-flight requests exceeding this are terminated.
[S3] The changelog notes that health-check propagation to the load balancer can lag by up to 10 seconds.
prompt: Why do clients see intermittent 503 responses during a rolling deploy?
reference: Offer the two documented mechanisms as candidates - health-check propagation lag of up to 10 seconds [S3] and termination of in-flight requests past the 30-second drain timeout [S2] - and state explicitly that the context does not diagnose the reported 503s.

context:
[S1] The API reference states that request bodies may not exceed 10 MB.
[S2] The migration guide published with v3 states that the request body limit was raised to 25 MB.
[S3] Both documents describe the same v3 API surface.
prompt: What is the maximum request body size accepted by the API?
reference: Conflict: 10 MB in the API reference [S1] versus 25 MB in the v3 migration guide [S2], both describing the same surface [S3]. Report both and flag that the reference is likely stale; do not silently pick one.

context:
[S1] Eventual reads are served from the nearest replica and may lag the primary by up to two seconds.
[S2] Strong reads are routed to the primary and always reflect all previously acknowledged writes.
[S3] Strong reads cost twice as many read units as eventual reads.
prompt: Which consistency mode should I use if a read must reflect a write I just made from the same client?
reference: Strong reads [S2], because they are routed to the primary and reflect all acknowledged writes. Note the eventual-read lag of up to two seconds [S1] and the 2x read-unit cost [S3]. No session-consistency mode is described, so do not offer one.

context:
[S1] Background jobs are terminated after 15 minutes of wall-clock execution.
[S2] Synchronous request handlers time out after 30 seconds.
[S3] Scheduled triggers fire at most once per minute.
[S4] Job logs are retained for 14 days.
prompt: How long can a background job run before the platform kills it?
reference: 15 minutes of wall-clock execution [S1]. The 30-second handler timeout [S2], the trigger cadence [S3] and log retention [S4] are unrelated limits.

context:
[S1] Release 4.0 introduced breaking changes to the authentication middleware.
[S2] Releases 4.1 through 4.6 are described as backward compatible in their summaries, though the summaries are abridged here.
[S3] A complete list of breaking changes is maintained in the upgrade matrix.
prompt: How many breaking changes were introduced across the 4.x releases?
reference: No count is derivable: 4.0's breaking changes are not enumerated [S1], the 4.1-4.6 summaries are abridged [S2], and the authoritative list is the upgrade matrix [S3]. Abstain with that pointer.

context:
[S1] The cache layer performs a synchronous write-through to the shared cache on every mutation.
[S2] Tenants in the shared tier contend for a single cache shard per region.
[S3] Benchmark results for the cache layer are published per release but are not included here.
prompt: Why does enabling the new cache layer increase p99 latency for some tenants?
reference: Give the mechanism from [S1] and [S2] - synchronous write-through on every mutation plus contention for one shared shard per region - explicitly as a hypothesis, and state that the context contains no latency measurements [S3]. Do not quote a magnitude.

context:
[S1] The electoral commission put first-round turnout at 61.2 percent.
[S2] Runoff turnout figures are still being compiled and are expected on Friday.
[S3] In the last comparable election, runoff turnout was four points below the first round.
prompt: Did turnout in the runoff exceed turnout in the first round?
reference: Not yet answerable for this election. Give first-round turnout, 61.2 percent [S1], state that the runoff figure is pending [S2], and refuse to transfer the four-point drop from a previous election [S3].

context:
[S1] The company's statement says the plant ceased production on 14 May.
[S2] The union's account, published the same week, says the last shift ran on 2 June and that production continued at reduced volume until then.
[S3] Both parties agree the formal closure notice was filed on 30 April.
prompt: When did the plant actually shut down?
reference: Conflicting dates: 14 May per the company [S1] versus 2 June per the union, with reduced-volume production until then [S2]. Only the 30 April closure notice is agreed [S3]. Report both with attribution.

context:
[S1] Authorities evacuated 1,240 residents from the eastern district on Tuesday.
[S2] A further 860 residents were evacuated from the riverside area on Wednesday.
[S3] No further evacuations were ordered after Wednesday, officials said.
prompt: How many people were evacuated in total?
reference: 2,100 in total: 1,240 on Tuesday [S1] plus 860 on Wednesday [S2], with [S3] closing the count. No voluntary departures are reported anywhere.

context:
[S1] The operator said services were suspended after a landslip covered 40 metres of track north of the junction.
[S2] Separately, a signalling fault caused delays of up to 25 minutes on the adjacent line the same morning.
[S3] A scheduled engineering possession is planned for the following weekend.
[S4] Passengers were advised to use replacement buses.
prompt: What caused the rail service suspension?
reference: A landslip covering 40 metres of track north of the junction [S1]. The signalling fault [S2] is described as separate and affected the adjacent line; the engineering possession [S3] and the bus advice [S4] are not causes.

context:
[S1] The parties reached a settlement on the eve of trial, ending a three-year dispute.
[S2] Terms of the settlement are confidential, both sides confirmed.
[S3] The plaintiff had originally sought damages of $40 million.
prompt: How much was the settlement?
reference: The amount is confidential and not disclosed [S2]. The $40 million in [S3] is the sum originally sought, not the settlement. Abstain and say so explicitly.

context:
[S1] The new stadium will seat 42,000.
[S2] The existing ground has been in continuous use since 1936 and is described by the club as no longer fit for purpose.
[S3] The new site is 12 hectares, roughly double the footprint of the current ground.
prompt: Is the new stadium bigger than the one it replaces?
reference: On footprint, yes: 12 hectares, roughly double the current ground [S3]. On seating, no comparison is possible - only the new capacity of 42,000 is given [S1] and the existing ground's capacity is not stated [S2]. Answer the comparable part and name the missing part.

context:
[S1] Mediators said the ceasefire took effect at midnight on 3 October.
[S2] A briefing from one of the parties dates the start of the ceasefire to 7 October, following a four-day negotiation over monitoring arrangements.
[S3] Both accounts describe the same agreement and the same monitoring mission.
prompt: How long has the ceasefire been in effect?
reference: The elapsed time depends on a disputed start date: 3 October per mediators [S1] versus 7 October per one party's briefing [S2], both describing the same agreement [S3]. Give both and do not compute a single figure.

context:
[S1] The first contract, for rolling stock maintenance, is worth 118 million.
[S2] The second, covering depot works, is worth 46 million.
[S3] The third, for signalling upgrades, is worth 91 million.
prompt: What was the total value of the three contracts awarded?
reference: 255 million: 118 [S1] plus 46 [S2] plus 91 [S3]. Nothing in the passages states contract durations, so do not add any.
